title: Training Process Animator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Step through gradient descent as it fits a line to study-hours data, and watch the weight, the bias, the gradients, and the training and validation error change at every iteration.

educational.topic: The training loop of a linear model
learningObjectives: Students will be able to explain how each iteration of training uses the error and its gradients to adjust a model's parameters, and predict how the learning rate changes the way training proceeds.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through of an iterative algorithm on concrete data with every intermediate value shown
keyQuestions: Why are the first updates large and the later ones small?
What do the signs of the two gradients tell you about how w and b will change?
Why does training end at the same line from every starting point?
The validation rows never enter the gradient. Why does the validation MSE still go down?
commonMisconceptions: The model sees the right answer and jumps to it (it only learns which direction lowers the error, and takes many steps).
Training changes the data (the points never move; only w and b change).
More iterations always keep improving the model (once the gradient is nearly zero, further updates change almost nothing).
The training MSE should reach zero (noise in the data sets a floor; here the lowest possible training MSE is about 0.55).
assessmentOpportunities: Students are given w, b, both gradients, and a learning rate for one iteration, compute the updated w and b, and explain in two sentences why the validation MSE is tracked even though it is never used in the update.
